meta.title: ILL Watch — Open-source Cyber Threat Intelligence platform
meta.description: ILL Watch collects threat intelligence, prioritises vulnerabilities, correlates and drives incident response. Open source, self-hosted, on a single server.

hero.title: See the threat before it sees you.
hero.lead: ILL Watch does the repetitive work of a SOC — collecting, deduplicating, prioritising, correlating — so your analysts keep only the decisions. On your own server, under the MIT licence.

problem.label: The problem
problem.title: Too many signals, too little time
problem.p1_text: Indicators copied from tool to tool, unreadable advisories, duplicate alerts: most of the time goes into sorting instead of deciding.
problem.p2_text: Commercial platforms cost tens of thousands per year; complete open-source alternatives require heavy infrastructure.
problem.p3_text: A published vulnerability is exploited within days, and regulations such as NIS 2 or DORA demand active monitoring and notification within 24 to 72 hours.

platform.label: The platform
platform.title: From raw feed to decision, in a single tool
platform.lead: Seven modules sharing the same data, the same severity scale and the same audit trail.
platform.feeds_text: CSV, JSON, STIX 2.1, TAXII 2.1, AlienVault OTX, abuse.ch… Indicators normalised, deduplicated, with their provenance and a confidence score.
platform.cve_text: NVD, CISA KEV and FIRST EPSS combined into a deterministic 0–100 score, broken down and explainable. An exploited CVE is never below P1.
platform.corr_text: Asset inventory matched against exploited CVEs and indicators, version by version: an alert is raised only if your version is affected.
platform.soc_text: NIST SP 800-61 lifecycle, immutable timeline, L1 → L3 tiers with justified escalation, MTTA and MTTR measured.
platform.hunt_text: Replay your logs against the whole database: Tor, dynamic DNS, generated domains (DGA), ransomware infrastructure.
platform.intel_text: MITRE ATT&CK techniques and actors, campaigns and attribution by infrastructure, STIX 2.1 sharing and a TAXII 2.1 server.
platform.obs_text: Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards, ten operational alerts and backup restores tested every month.

sim.label: Try it
sim.title: CVE priority simulator
sim.lead: The same formula as the ILL Watch engine. Adjust the signals and watch the priority change.
sim.epss_help: Probability of exploitation in the next 30 days
sim.floor: KEV floor: an actively exploited vulnerability is ranked at least P1, whatever its score.
sim.formula: Score = CVSS × 3 + EPSS × 25 + KEV × 25 + exploit × 10 + ransomware × 10, capped at 100. P0 ≥ 80 · P1 ≥ 60 · P2 ≥ 40.
sim.noscript: The simulator needs JavaScript; the formula below still applies.

how.label: How it works
how.title: One pipeline, six steps, one audit trail
how.s1_text: Public and private feeds, each at its own pace, with automatic back-off for failing sources.
how.s2_text: One format, deduplicated; every indicator keeps all of its sources.
how.s3_text: Country and autonomous system offline, confidence computed and explained.
how.s4_text: Indicators × CVEs × assets × versions: only what concerns you.
how.s5_text: Deterministic P0 to P3 score, alert when the threshold is crossed.
how.s6_text: Incident opened in one click, escalated, closed, traced end to end.

trust.label: Trust
trust.title: Verifiable, not just claimed
trust.open_text: All the code is public under the MIT licence. No black box, no vendor lock-in.
trust.ci_text: More than {tests} tests against a real PostgreSQL database, {coverage}% coverage, strict typing.
trust.real_text: A complete instance is rebuilt every Monday and checked against real sources.
trust.scan_text: Image, code and Git history scanned: no critical vulnerability, no secret.
trust.self_text: Self-hosted on a single server; offline enrichment, no third-party service.
trust.light_text: Under {memory} MB of memory; dashboard in {dashboard} s over half a million indicators.

roadmap.label: Roadmap
roadmap.title: A project driven by measured milestones
roadmap.lead: A milestone is closed when its criteria are measured, not when the code is merged.
